cards.says: The war in the west had become a deadlock of shelling and trenches.
Falkenhayn, Germany's top general, had no way to win by attacking.
Frontal attacks won almost no ground and killed huge numbers of men.
Falkenhayn looked for a new kind of battle and wrote down his idea.
In his memoirs he claimed the plan was to bleed the French army, not break it.
cards.title: FALKENHAYN — AS HE WROTE AFTER THE WAR

cards.says: The French line held everywhere; no breakthrough was possible.
The idea: make France pour men into one place until it ran out of them.
Choose a place France must defend and let German artillery kill the defenders.

cards.at: The place he picked was Verdun
cards.says: He chose Verdun, a fortress town on the Meuse that France would never give up.
cards.label: VERDUN

cards.says: German storm troops attacked Verdun in the snow in February 1916.
Verdun became a battle of endurance lasting about 300 days.
The plan failed because German attackers died almost as fast as the French.
Both armies lost well over 300,000 men at Verdun.
cards.title: VERDUN 1916 — CASUALTIES (ONE ESTIMATE)

cards.says: Verdun consumed about seventy thousand men every month for most of a year.

cards.at: The army that was supposed to bleed
cards.says: The German army bled at Verdun just as badly as the French.
Meanwhile the Allies attacked in two other places, east and west.
cards.label: BRUSILOV

cards.says: Brusilov planned a broad Russian offensive in the east.
Russian troops attacked along a wide front and broke the Austro-Hungarian army.
The Austro-Hungarians lost so many men that their army never recovered.

cards.at: Germany had to send divisions east
cards.says: German troop trains left for the east to rescue the collapsing Austrians.
Romania joined the war on the Allied side.
cards.label: ROMANIA JOINS THE ALLIES

cards.says: On 1 July the British went over the top on the Somme.
The first day cost the British army over fifty-seven thousand men killed or wounded.
Almost twenty thousand British soldiers were killed that day.
It remains the deadliest day the British Army has ever had.
cards.label: WORST DAY IN BRITISH ARMY HISTORY

cards.says: The Somme dragged on for 141 days in rain and mud.
The German defenders suffered terribly under the British guns.
The British sent the first tanks in history into battle and the Germans fled.
